questions.question: Will María Corina Machado physically return to Venezuela between May 10, 2026, and July 1, 2026?
questions.background:
María Corina Machado is a Venezuelan opposition leader and 2025 Nobel Peace Prize laureate who has been living in exile since leaving Venezuela in December 2025. She has been primarily based in the United States, with travel to Europe for public appearances. As of April 20, 2026 (UTC), she was in Madrid, Spain, where she told Reuters she "absolutely" sees herself back in Venezuela soon and expects to return before the end of 2026, though she did not set a specific date [Venezuela's Machado plans to return home by end of year, urges ...](https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/venezuelas-machado-plans-return-home-by-end-year-urges-swift-elections-2026-04-20/). In early March 2026, she stated she would return "within the next few weeks," but as of May 2026 she has not yet done so. Her return is described as "the real test" of Venezuela's political opening following the January 2026 capture of Nicolás Maduro by U.S. forces. The current Venezuelan government, led by Delcy Rodríguez, has not explicitly guaranteed her safe return. Reports indicate Trump advised Machado not to return immediately, and she is coordinating closely with the U.S. on the timing.

The GJOpen forecasting market for "Will María Corina Machado publicly return to Venezuela before 20 June 2026?" has shown approximately 17% probability, reflecting significant skepticism that her return will happen on this timeline despite her stated intentions. Key factors include: U.S.-Venezuela diplomatic dynamics, the Rodríguez government's tolerance, security risks to Machado, and opposition electoral strategy considerations.
questions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves **Yes** if María Corina Machado is confirmed to have physically returned to Venezuelan territory (i.e., physical presence on Venezuelan soil, including its mainland, islands, and territorial waters as defined by the map at https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geography_of_Venezuela) on or after May 10, 2026 (00:00 UTC) and on or before July 1, 2026 (23:59 UTC).

"Physically return" means that Machado is confirmed to be bodily present on Venezuelan territory — this includes arrival by land, air, or sea. Brief transits (e.g., a plane refueling stop without disembarking) do not count; she must disembark or otherwise set foot on Venezuelan soil.

This question resolves **No** if no such confirmed return occurs within the specified window.

**Resolution sources:** Credible reporting from at least one major international news agency, such as Reuters (https://www.reuters.com), Associated Press (https://apnews.com), or Agence France-Presse (https://www.afp.com), confirming her physical presence in Venezuela. Reporting from BBC, The New York Times, or The Washington Post would also suffice. Given Machado's global profile as a Nobel laureate and major opposition figure, any return to Venezuela would be widely reported by these outlets.

questions.question: Will the Courts and Tribunals Bill complete its Report stage in the House of Commons by July 1, 2026?
questions.background:
The Courts and Tribunals Bill is a UK Government bill currently progressing through the House of Commons. The bill passed its Second Reading on March 10, 2026, by a vote of 304-203, with 10 Labour MPs voting against the government, and reports suggesting up to 65 Labour MPs were considering rebellion over the removal of jury trial rights in either-way cases. The Committee stage concluded on April 28, 2026 [https://bills.parliament.uk/bills/4083/stages](https://bills.parliament.uk/bills/4083/stages). As of May 12, 2026, the Report stage is listed as "Date to be announced" on the official UK Parliament bill tracker [https://bills.parliament.uk/bills/4083/stages](https://bills.parliament.uk/bills/4083/stages).

The combination of scheduling uncertainty—with no announced date for Report stage—and the potential for a significant Labour rebellion creates genuine uncertainty about whether the government will bring this bill back to the floor of the House of Commons for its Report stage before July 1, 2026. Government business managers must balance parliamentary time constraints, potential amendments, and internal party management.
questions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves **Yes** if the Report stage of the Courts and Tribunals Bill is completed in the House of Commons on or after May 12, 2026, and no later than July 1, 2026, at 23:59 UTC. It resolves **No** otherwise.

"Report stage" refers to the stage of legislative proceedings in the House of Commons where the whole House considers amendments to a bill after Committee stage, as defined by the UK Parliament glossary: https://www.parliament.uk/site-information/glossary/report-stage/

Completion of the Report stage is defined as the House of Commons concluding its report stage proceedings, such that the bill is ready for its Third Reading. This will be determined by the official UK Parliament bill tracker at https://bills.parliament.uk/bills/4083/stages showing a completed Report stage with a date on or before July 1, 2026.

questions.question: Will Cerebras Systems' shares begin trading on Nasdaq on or after May 1, 2026, and by June 1, 2026?
questions.background:

A company spokesperson indicated a target of "mid-May" 2026 for the offering [https://techcrunch.com/2026/04/18/ai-chip-startup-cerebras-files-for-ipo/](https://techcrunch.com/2026/04/18/ai-chip-startup-cerebras-files-for-ipo/).

However, Cerebras has a history of IPO delays. The company previously announced plans for an IPO in 2024 but withdrew its paperwork in October 2025, citing the need to provide updated information on its financial performance and strategy [https://www.cnbc.com/2026/04/17/cerebras-new-ipo-ai-chips.html](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/04/17/cerebras-new-ipo-ai-chips.html). This prior withdrawal introduces meaningful uncertainty about whether the current attempt will proceed on schedule.

Cerebras reported $510 million in revenue in 2025 (76% year-over-year growth) and has secured major partnerships, including a deal with Amazon Web Services and a partnership with OpenAI reportedly valued at over $10–20 billion [https://techcrunch.com/2026/04/18/ai-chip-startup-cerebras-files-for-ipo/](https://techcrunch.com/2026/04/18/ai-chip-startup-cerebras-files-for-ipo/)[https://www.cnbc.com/2026/04/17/cerebras-new-ipo-ai-chips.html](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/04/17/cerebras-new-ipo-ai-chips.html). As of May 1, 2026, the SEC registration statement has not yet become effective and shares are not yet trading.
questions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves **Yes** if Cerebras Systems' shares (ticker: CBRS) have their first trade on the Nasdaq stock exchange at any point on or after May 1, 2026, and on or before June 1, 2026, 11:59 PM ET.

This question resolves **No** if:
- Cerebras has not begun trading on Nasdaq by 11:59 PM ET on June 1, 2026, or
- Cerebras withdraws its IPO filing before that deadline.

"Shares begin trading" is defined as the first completed trade of Cerebras common stock on the Nasdaq exchange, as reported by the Nasdaq IPO calendar (https://www.nasdaq.com/market-activity/ipos) or SEC EDGAR filings (https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&company=cerebras&CIK=&type=S-1&dateb=&owner=include&count=40&search_text=&action=getcompany). Confirmation from major financial news outlets (e.g., CNBC, Reuters, Bloomberg) reporting that trading has commenced will also be accepted as a resolution source.

questions.question: Will Toshiaki Takahashi (高橋敏明) win the Saijo City (西条市) mayoral election on May 17, 2026?
questions.background:
On March 18, 2026, the Saijo City (西条市) municipal assembly in Ehime Prefecture, Japan, passed a no-confidence vote against Mayor Toshiaki Takahashi (高橋敏明, age 67) over allegations of power harassment. Rather than dissolving the assembly, Takahashi chose not to contest the decision, resulting in his automatic loss of the mayoral position on March 29, 2026. A special mayoral election was subsequently called for May 17, 2026.

The race is a two-candidate contest between Takahashi, running as the former mayor (前職), and Mitsuyoshi Ochi (越智光好, age 61), the former deputy mayor running as a newcomer (新人). Takahashi is effectively betting that voters will side with him over the city council that ousted him. A notable precedent is Hyogo Governor Saito's successful re-election after a similar scandal-driven ouster, though outcomes in such races are far from predetermined.

Early voting has already begun. Official results will be available on election night, May 17, 2026.

Sources: [go2senkyo.com](https://go2senkyo.com/local/senkyo/28647), [FNN](https://www.fnn.jp/articles/-/1042738).
questions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves **Yes** if Toshiaki Takahashi (高橋敏明) receives the plurality of votes cast in the Saijo City (西条市) mayoral election held on May 17, 2026, as determined by the official election authority (Saijo City Election Commission).

Resolution will be based on official election results as reported by the Saijo City official website (https://www.city.saijo.ehime.jp/) or credible Japanese news outlets such as NHK (https://www.nhk.or.jp/), FNN, or the election tracking site go2senkyo.com (https://go2senkyo.com/local/senkyo/28647).

**Special conditions:**
- If the election scheduled for May 17, 2026, is postponed to a date on or before July 1, 2026, resolution will be based on the results of the rescheduled election.
- If the election is postponed beyond July 1, 2026, or canceled entirely, this question resolves **No**.
- If Toshiaki Takahashi does not appear on the final ballot (e.g., due to withdrawal or disqualification), this question resolves **No**.

questions.question: Will San Francisco Proposition C receive more total "Yes" votes than Proposition D in the June 2, 2026 election?
questions.background:
San Francisco's June 2, 2026 ballot features two competing business tax measures related to the city's "CEO pay gap" tax — a tax on businesses where the top executive earns more than 100 times the median employee's compensation.

**Proposition C** (backed by the SF Chamber of Commerce and business groups) would raise the gross receipts tax exemption threshold from $5 million to $7.5 million and accelerate a planned tax rate increase from 2028 to 2027. It is projected to *decrease* city revenue by $30–$40 million annually [https://missionlocal.org/2026/05/sf-june-election-2026-ballot/](https://missionlocal.org/2026/05/sf-june-election-2026-ballot/). (Official text: https://www.sf.gov/information/proposition-c-june-2-2026; Ballotpedia: https://ballotpedia.org/San_Francisco,_California,_Measure_C,_Gross_Receipts_Tax_Exemption_and_Top_Executive_Pay_Tax_Increase_Initiative_(June_2026))

**Proposition D** (backed by the SF Labor Council, labor unions, and progressive figures including Bernie Sanders) would increase taxes on businesses subject to the CEO pay gap tax. It is projected to *increase* city revenue by $200–$300 million annually [https://missionlocal.org/2026/05/sf-june-election-2026-ballot/](https://missionlocal.org/2026/05/sf-june-election-2026-ballot/). (Official text: https://www.sf.gov/changes-to-business-tax; Ballotpedia: https://ballotpedia.org/San_Francisco,_California,_Measure_D,_Changes_to_Top_Executive_Pay_Tax_Initiative_(June_2026))

These measures are competing: if both pass, the one receiving more "Yes" votes takes effect while the other is nullified [https://missionlocal.org/2026/05/sf-june-election-2026-ballot/](https://missionlocal.org/2026/05/sf-june-election-2026-ballot/). This makes the relative vote count — not just passage — the decisive outcome. Polls close at 8:00 PM Pacific Time (PT) on June 2, 2026.
questions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves **Yes** if the total number of "Yes" votes cast for Proposition C exceeds the total number of "Yes" votes cast for Proposition D in the June 2, 2026 San Francisco Consolidated Statewide Direct Primary Election, as reported by the San Francisco Department of Elections.

It resolves **No** if Proposition D receives an equal or greater number of "Yes" votes than Proposition C.

Resolution will be based on official results published by the San Francisco Department of Elections at https://www.sf.gov/election-results (or the legacy URL https://www.sfelections.org/results). Results need not be formally certified; the most recent official count posted by the Department of Elections by the resolution date will be used, provided the Department considers results sufficiently final for reporting (i.e., not a "zero report"). If no results beyond a zero report are available by July 1, 2026, resolution is deferred until results are posted.

questions.question: Will the Central Bank of the Republic of Türkiye (CBRT) raise its policy rate at the June 2026 MPC meeting?
questions.background: The Central Bank of the Republic of Türkiye (CBRT) uses the one-week repo auction rate as its primary policy instrument (the "policy rate"), as defined in its [Monetary Policy for 2026 document](https://tcmb.gov.tr/wps/wcm/connect/c2ac62b6-3112-4f33-a6ad-3817defff0be/December28.pdf?MOD=AJPERES). As of the most recent Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) decision on April 22, 2026 (Press Release 2026-17), the policy rate stands at 37% [Press Release on Interest Rates (2026-17) - TCMB](https://www.tcmb.gov.tr/wps/wcm/connect/EN/TCMB+EN/MPC/MPC+Meeting+Decisions). The CBRT had previously cut rates by a cumulative 900 basis points from a peak of 50%, but paused its easing cycle amid persistent inflation. Turkey's annual inflation has been running above 30%, and Citi has warned that an additional rate hike may be needed. Reuters has reported that some investors see a rate hike as possible. The next MPC meeting is scheduled for June 11, 2026, which is the only meeting between now and July 1, 2026. The 2026 MPC calendar is published at the [CBRT calendar page](https://www.tcmb.gov.tr/wps/wcm/connect/en/tcmb+en/main+menu/announcements/calendar). A rate hike after months of easing would represent a dramatic policy reversal and a signal of institutional independence in the face of political pressure to keep rates low.
questions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves **Yes** if, on or after May 12, 2026 (Turkey Time, TRT/UTC+3), the CBRT announces that the one-week repo auction rate (the policy rate) has been set to a level strictly greater than the rate in effect immediately prior to that announcement. As of May 12, 2026, the rate in effect is 37%.

This question resolves **No** if no such increase is announced by July 1, 2026, 23:59 TRT (UTC+3).

The resolution source is the official CBRT "Press Releases on Interest Rates" page: https://www.tcmb.gov.tr/wps/wcm/connect/EN/TCMB+EN/MPC/MPC+Meeting+Decisions

If the CBRT changes its primary policy instrument from the one-week repo auction rate to a different instrument, the question will resolve based on the successor instrument as officially designated by the CBRT. If no MPC meeting takes place during the resolution window, the question resolves **No**.

questions.question: Will the SAF maintain control of Kurmuk (Blue Nile State) through June 1, 2026?
questions.background: Kurmuk is a town in Blue Nile State, Sudan, that has been a focal point of fighting during the Sudanese civil war. The town has changed hands multiple times in 2026: the RSF and SPLM-N (al-Hilu) seized Kurmuk on March 24, 2026, before the SAF claimed to retake it on April 20, 2026 [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_the_Sudanese_civil_war_(2026)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_the_Sudanese_civil_war_(2026)). Just days later, on April 25, 2026, the RSF claimed to have taken the nearby town of Al-Kaili, indicating the Blue Nile front remains highly active and contested [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_the_Sudanese_civil_war_(2026)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_the_Sudanese_civil_war_(2026)). As of April 29, 2026, the SAF is reported to hold Kurmuk, but the rapid back-and-forth in the area makes continued control uncertain. Kurmuk is strategically significant as it sits near the Ethiopian border and controls key supply routes into Blue Nile State.
questions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves **Yes** if, as of June 1, 2026 at 23:59 UTC, the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) are assessed to hold the town center of Kurmuk (approximately 10.55°N, 34.28°E) in Blue Nile State, Sudan — meaning there is no credible reporting that opposing forces (RSF, SPLM-N, or allied militias) have captured or established primary military/administrative control over the town center at any point between April 29, 2026 and June 1, 2026 at 23:59 UTC.

The question resolves **No** if credible sources report that opposing forces captured or established primary control over Kurmuk town center at any point during this period, even if the SAF subsequently retook it.

"Control" is defined as having the primary military presence in and administrative authority over the town center of Kurmuk, such that opposing forces are not able to freely operate within it.

Resolution will be determined by the preponderance of evidence from credible sources including: ACLED (https://acleddata.com/), Sudan War Monitor, Sudan Tribune (https://sudantribune.com/), Radio Dabanga (https://www.dabangasudan.org/), and major international wire services (Reuters, AP, AFP). If sources conflict, the consensus among these sources will be used.

questions.question: Will OpenAI make GPT-5.5 available to free-tier ChatGPT users by June 1, 2026?
questions.background:
On April 23, 2026, OpenAI released GPT-5.5 (codenamed "Spud"), its newest frontier model [Introducing GPT-5.5 - OpenAI](https://openai.com/index/introducing-gpt-5-5/). At launch, GPT-5.5 was made available to ChatGPT Plus, Pro, Business, and Enterprise users, but not to free-tier users [Introducing GPT-5.5 - OpenAI](https://openai.com/index/introducing-gpt-5-5/). API access, initially withheld at launch, was enabled on April 24, 2026 [GPT-5.5 - Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GPT-5.5).

As of April 29, 2026, free-tier ChatGPT users remain on GPT-5.3 Instant and do not have access to GPT-5.5 (see https://fritz.ai/chatgpt-pricing/ and https://help.openai.com/en/articles/11909943-gpt-5-1-in-chatgpt). OpenAI has not announced a specific timeline for bringing GPT-5.5 to the free tier.

OpenAI has historically rolled out new models to paid tiers first, with free-tier access following weeks to months later. For reference, GPT-5.5 pricing in the API is $5/1M input tokens and $30/1M output tokens [https://openai.com/api/pricing/](https://openai.com/api/pricing/), suggesting significant compute costs that may delay free-tier availability.

Note: The original question about GPT-5.5 public API availability has already resolved, as OpenAI made GPT-5.5 available in the API on April 24, 2026 [Introducing GPT-5.5 - OpenAI](https://openai.com/index/introducing-gpt-5-5/). This reformulated question focuses on the still-uncertain free-tier rollout.
questions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves as **Yes** if, at any point between April 29, 2026 (00:00 UTC) and June 1, 2026 (23:59 UTC), OpenAI makes any version of GPT-5.5 (including GPT-5.5 Thinking or GPT-5.5 Pro) selectable or usable by users on the free tier of ChatGPT (https://chatgpt.com).

"Free tier" refers to the $0/month ChatGPT plan as described on OpenAI's ChatGPT pricing page (https://openai.com/chatgpt/pricing/). "Available" means free-tier users can select and use GPT-5.5 for conversations, even if subject to rate limits or usage caps.

This question resolves as **No** if, by 23:59 UTC on June 1, 2026, GPT-5.5 remains unavailable to free-tier ChatGPT users.

Resolution source: The OpenAI Help Center article on GPT-5.5 in ChatGPT (https://help.openai.com/en/articles/11909943-gpt-5-1-in-chatgpt), the OpenAI ChatGPT pricing page (https://openai.com/chatgpt/pricing/), or credible reporting from outlets such as TechCrunch (https://techcrunch.com), The Verge, or Reuters confirming free-tier access.

questions.question: Will China officially confirm President Xi Jinping's attendance at the 2026 BRICS Summit in India by June 1, 2026?
questions.background:
India assumed the 2026 BRICS presidency on January 1, 2026, and is scheduled to host the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi in August–September 2026. During a bilateral meeting on the sidelines of the SCO Summit in Tianjin, China, in late 2025, Prime Minister Narendra Modi invited Chinese President Xi Jinping to attend the summit. Xi thanked Modi for the invitation, and various reports described Xi as having "accepted" it.

However, accepting a diplomatic invitation and formally confirming attendance are distinct. As of May 1, 2026, there has been no official confirmation from the Chinese government that Xi Jinping will personally attend the BRICS Summit in India. Reports describe Xi as "likely attending," which would mark his first visit to India since 2019. Russia's President Putin has reportedly confirmed his attendance.

India-China relations remain in a state of "fragile tranquility." While both countries agreed to support each other's BRICS presidencies (India in 2026, China in 2027) and have engaged in diplomatic dialogue—including China's Vice Foreign Minister attending the first BRICS Sherpa meeting in New Delhi in February 2026—unresolved territorial disputes along the Himalayan border and broader geopolitical dynamics (including US-India-China triangular relations and Dalai Lama succession tensions) introduce uncertainty about whether Xi will formally commit to attending within this timeframe.

The BRICS 2026 official website is https://www.brics2026.gov.in/. China's Ministry of Foreign Affairs publishes statements at https://www.fmprc.gov.cn/eng/.
questions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves **Yes** if, on or after May 1, 2026, and on or before 23:59 UTC on June 1, 2026, there is an official confirmation that Chinese President Xi Jinping will personally attend the 2026 BRICS Summit in India.

**"Official confirmation"** is defined as any of the following:
1. A statement published by the Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs (https://www.fmprc.gov.cn/eng/) confirming Xi Jinping's planned attendance at the 2026 BRICS Summit in India; OR
2. A statement published by the Indian Ministry of External Affairs (https://www.mea.gov.in/) confirming that China has confirmed Xi Jinping's attendance; OR
3. A credible report by at least two of the following major news agencies—Reuters, Associated Press (AP), or Agence France-Presse (AFP)—stating that China has officially confirmed Xi Jinping's attendance.

Merely reiterating that Xi "accepted the invitation" or that he is "expected to attend" does not count as official confirmation. The confirmation must specifically state that Xi Jinping will attend (or "plans to attend" / "is confirmed to attend") the summit.

If no such official confirmation is issued by 23:59 UTC on June 1, 2026, the question resolves **No**.

questions.question: Will the U.S. House of Representatives pass the KIDS Act (H.R. 7757) by June 1, 2026?
questions.background:
H.R. 7757, the Kids Internet and Digital Safety (KIDS) Act, was introduced in the U.S. House of Representatives on March 3, 2026, by Rep. Brett Guthrie [Actions - H.R.7757 - 119th Congress (2025-2026): KIDS Act](https://www.congress.gov/bill/119th-congress/house-bill/7757/all-actions). The bill aims to protect children and teens online, empower parents, and strengthen families. It incorporates several related measures including the Kids Online Safety Act (KOSA) and the AI Warnings And Resources for Education (AWARE) Act.

As of May 1, 2026, the bill has been referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce and the House Committee on the Judiciary [Actions - H.R.7757 - 119th Congress (2025-2026): KIDS Act](https://www.congress.gov/bill/119th-congress/house-bill/7757/all-actions). The House Energy and Commerce Committee has advanced the bill along party lines to a full House vote. However, no further floor action has been recorded on congress.gov as of this date [Actions - H.R.7757 - 119th Congress (2025-2026): KIDS Act](https://www.congress.gov/bill/119th-congress/house-bill/7757/all-actions).

Child online safety has bipartisan support in concept, and Senate companion legislation (S. 1748, the Kids Online Safety Act) also exists. However, House floor scheduling remains uncertain given competing legislative priorities, and the bill still needs to clear the Judiciary Committee or receive a discharge/waiver. The gap between committee passage and a full House floor vote makes the outcome within this timeframe genuinely uncertain.
questions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves **Yes** if H.R. 7757 (the KIDS Act, 119th Congress) is passed by the U.S. House of Representatives on or after April 30, 2026, and no later than June 1, 2026, at 11:59 PM UTC.

"Passed" means the bill receives a favorable vote by the full House of Representatives, whether by recorded vote, voice vote, or passage under suspension of the rules. The definitive resolution source is the bill's official actions page on Congress.gov: https://www.congress.gov/bill/119th-congress/house-bill/7757/all-actions

The question resolves **Yes** if that page shows an action indicating passage by the House (e.g., "Passed/agreed to in House") dated on or before June 1, 2026 (UTC). If no such action appears by that date, the question resolves **No**.

questions.question: Will Mike Collins win the 2026 Georgia Republican U.S. Senate nomination?
questions.background:
The 2026 Georgia Republican U.S. Senate primary is scheduled for May 19, 2026, with a potential runoff on June 16, 2026. The winner will face incumbent Democratic Senator Jon Ossoff in the November 3, 2026 general election. Under Georgia law, if no candidate receives more than 50% of the vote in the primary, the top two candidates advance to a runoff.

U.S. Representative Mike Collins is the polling frontrunner but faces significant competition from former U.S. Representative Buddy Carter and former University of Tennessee football coach Derek Dooley. According to the RealClearPolling average (based on polls through May 2, 2026), Collins leads with approximately 28.3%, with individual polls showing him between 23% and 33% [2026 Georgia Senate - Republican Primary - RealClearPolling](https://www.realclearpolling.com/polls/senate/republican-primary/2026/georgia). The most recent Quantus Insights poll (April 28–May 2, 2026) placed Collins at 33% [2026 Georgia Senate - Republican Primary - RealClearPolling](https://www.realclearpolling.com/polls/senate/republican-primary/2026/georgia). An Atlanta Journal-Constitution poll (April 18–26) showed Collins at 23%, and an InsiderAdvantage poll (April 22–23) had him at 27% [2026 Georgia Senate - Republican Primary - RealClearPolling](https://www.realclearpolling.com/polls/senate/republican-primary/2026/georgia).

With no candidate close to the 50% threshold needed to win outright, a runoff between the top two finishers is highly likely. In a runoff scenario, consolidation dynamics become crucial — supporters of eliminated candidates could unite behind Collins's opponent, potentially flipping the result. Over half of Republican primary voters remain undecided, adding significant uncertainty.
questions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves **Yes** if Mike Collins is certified as the Republican nominee for the 2026 U.S. Senate race in Georgia. This question resolves **No** if any other candidate is certified as the Republican nominee.

Resolution is based on official results from the **Georgia Secretary of State's elections results page** (https://sos.ga.gov/page/georgia-election-results), or the enhanced voting results portal (https://app.enhancedvoting.com/results/public/Georgia).

Specifically:
- If Collins wins more than 50% of the vote in the **May 19, 2026 primary** (results expected by 11:59 PM Eastern Time on May 19, 2026), the question resolves **Yes** at that point.
- If no candidate wins more than 50% and a **runoff is held on June 16, 2026**, the question resolves based on the certified runoff results. If Collins wins the runoff, it resolves **Yes**; if he loses, it resolves **No**.
- If Collins withdraws from the race before the primary or runoff, the question resolves **No**.

A "win" means being the candidate certified by the Georgia Secretary of State as the Republican nominee for the 2026 U.S. Senate general election.

questions.question: Will Mojtaba Khamenei deliver a live video or audio address by June 1, 2026?
questions.background:
Following the killing of his father, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, in March 2026, Mojtaba Khamenei was announced as Iran's new Supreme Leader. Since taking power, he has not appeared publicly or delivered any verified live address. All communications attributed to him have been delivered via proxy readers on Iranian state television, posted as written text, or released as AI-generated videos [Iran's new supreme leader is nowhere to be seen. That ...](https://www.cnn.com/2026/04/21/middleeast/iran-supreme-leader-intl).

On April 6, 2026, Iranian state-affiliated accounts released an AI-generated video purporting to show Mojtaba Khamenei entering a military command center, which was widely identified as fabricated by international media and fact-checkers. On April 21–23, 2026, CNN reported that Khamenei sustained significant injuries in the same strikes that killed his father—including facial lacerations and other wounds—and that he "struggles to speak" due to these injuries [Iran's new supreme leader is nowhere to be seen. That ...](https://www.cnn.com/2026/04/21/middleeast/iran-supreme-leader-intl). Reuters has also reported severe disfiguring wounds. Analysts suggest the regime is using his invisibility as a deliberate strategy while navigating ceasefire negotiations with the United States, but questions persist about whether he is capable of governing or communicating publicly.
questions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves **Yes** if Mojtaba Khamenei delivers a live video or audio address on or after the question's open date and on or before June 1, 2026, 23:59 UTC.

Key definitions:

- **"Live video or audio address"**: A real-time broadcast, or a verified recording, in which Mojtaba Khamenei is personally and recognizably speaking. This includes pre-recorded messages provided the recording is verified as authentic (i.e., not generated or synthesized by AI). The address must feature his actual voice and/or likeness, not a text overlay or subtitled silent footage.

- **"AI-generated"**: Any video or audio content created or substantially altered using artificial intelligence tools (e.g., deepfakes, voice synthesis, AI avatars). If credible sources (see below) report that an address is AI-generated or its authenticity is widely disputed by experts and major news outlets, it does not count toward resolution.

- **"Proxy"**: A third party (e.g., a state TV presenter, aide, or official) reading or conveying a message on Khamenei's behalf. Statements read by others on state television do not count.

The address must be confirmed as authentic by at least one of the following credible sources: IRNA (Islamic Republic News Agency, https://en.irna.ir/), BBC (https://www.bbc.com/), Reuters (https://www.reuters.com/), the Associated Press (AP, https://apnews.com/), or CNN (https://www.cnn.com/).

If no such verified live address occurs on or before June 1, 2026, this question resolves **No**.

questions.question: Will the FBI or DOJ announce the arrest of at least one individual connected to the March 2026 IoT botnet disruption operation by June 1, 2026?
questions.background:
On March 19, 2026, the U.S. Department of Justice, in coordination with authorities in Canada and Germany, dismantled the online infrastructure behind four major IoT botnets — Aisuru, Kimwolf, JackSkid, and Mossad — which had compromised over 3 million devices worldwide and were responsible for record-breaking DDoS attacks reaching 31.4 Tbps (https://www.justice.gov/usao-ak/pr/authorities-disrupt-worlds-largest-iot-ddos-botnets-responsible-record-breaking-attacks). No arrests were announced at the time of the operation [Feds Disrupt IoT Botnets Behind Huge DDoS Attacks](https://krebsonsecurity.com/2026/03/feds-disrupt-iot-botnets-behind-huge-ddos-attacks/).

KrebsOnSecurity identified two primary suspects: a 22-year-old Canadian man described as a core operator of the Kimwolf botnet, and a 15-year-old residing in Germany [Feds Disrupt IoT Botnets Behind Huge DDoS Attacks](https://krebsonsecurity.com/2026/03/feds-disrupt-iot-botnets-behind-huge-ddos-attacks/). German police confirmed they had identified two suspected administrators who would face legal proceedings. As of early April 2026, Canadian law enforcement — the OPP and Sûreté du Québec — confirmed they are conducting active investigations related to the dismantled networks. Cryptocurrency was reportedly seized in connection with the probe. As of May 2, 2026, no arrest of the Canadian suspect or any other individual has been officially announced by the FBI or DOJ in connection with this operation. The investigation remains ongoing, with cross-border law enforcement cooperation between the U.S., Canada, and Germany continuing.
questions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves **Yes** if the U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) or U.S. Department of Justice (DOJ) publishes an official press release or announcement confirming the [arrest](https://www.law.cornell.edu/wex/arrest) (i.e., the taking of a person into custody by legal authority) of at least one individual [connected to](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Complicity) (i.e., charged with, indicted for, or officially named as a participant in) the March 19, 2026 IoT botnet disruption operation targeting the Aisuru, Kimwolf, JackSkid, and/or Mossad botnets, as originally announced by the DOJ at https://www.justice.gov/usao-ak/pr/authorities-disrupt-worlds-largest-iot-ddos-botnets-responsible-record-breaking-attacks.

The official announcement of the arrest must be published on or after May 1, 2026, and by June 1, 2026 (23:59 UTC).

Primary resolution sources are:
- FBI press releases: https://www.fbi.gov/news/press-releases
- DOJ press releases: https://www.justice.gov/news

If no such announcement appears on these pages by the resolution deadline, the question resolves **No**.

questions.question: Will the Bank of Mexico's June 25, 2026, Monetary Policy Decision Be a Unanimous (5-0) Vote?
questions.background:
The Bank of Mexico (Banco de México, or "Banxico") sets monetary policy through its five-member Governing Board (Junta de Gobierno), composed of Governor Victoria Rodríguez Ceja and Deputy Governors Jonathan Heath, Galia Borja Gómez, Omar Mejía Castelazo, and José Gabriel Cuadra García (https://www.banxico.org.mx/getting-to-know-banco-de-mexico/board-of-governors-curriculum.html).

At its May 7, 2026, meeting, Banxico cut the overnight interbank interest rate by 25 basis points to 6.50% in a 3-2 split vote. Governor Rodríguez, Deputy Governors Cuadra and Mejía voted for the cut, while Deputy Governors Borja and Heath voted to hold rates unchanged. Banxico signaled this was the final cut in a two-year easing cycle that brought rates down 475 basis points from 11.25%.

With the easing cycle now declared over, the June 25, 2026, meeting is widely expected to feature a hold at 6.50%. However, the question of unanimity remains uncertain: the two dissenters (Borja and Heath) who wanted to hold in May may now agree with a hold decision, producing unanimity—or dovish members could push for further easing, maintaining a split. Recent Banxico decisions have frequently featured divided votes (the March 2026 cut was also a split decision), making unanimity genuinely uncertain.

The next scheduled monetary policy announcement is June 25, 2026, at 13:00 Central Time (CT, UTC-6).
questions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves **Yes** if the official monetary policy press release published by Banco de México (Banxico) on June 25, 2026, reports that the Governing Board's (Junta de Gobierno's) decision was reached by a **unanimous 5-0 vote**—meaning all five members of the Board voted for the same policy action (whether a hold, cut, or hike).

This question resolves **No** if the press release reports any vote split (e.g., 4-1, 3-2) or if the announcement is postponed beyond June 30, 2026 (UTC-6).

**Definitions:**
- "Unanimous" means all five sitting members of the Governing Board voted for the identical policy action, i.e., a 5-0 vote with no dissents.
- The "Governing Board" (Junta de Gobierno) is Banxico's five-member decision-making body as described at https://www.banxico.org.mx/getting-to-know-banco-de-mexico/board-of-governors-curriculum.html. It consists of one Governor and four Deputy Governors.
- If a Board vacancy reduces the voting members below five, a unanimous vote among all present members still counts as "Yes."

**Resolution source:** The official Banxico monetary policy statement for the June 25, 2026, decision, published at https://www.banxico.org.mx/publications-and-press/announcements-of-monetary-policy-decisions/monetary-policy-announcements.html. The vote breakdown is reported within the full text of the press release (PDF linked from that page).

questions.question: Will the Bank of Japan raise its short-term policy interest rate at the June 15–16, 2026 Monetary Policy Meeting?
questions.background:
As of May 13, 2026, the Bank of Japan (BOJ) maintains its short-term policy interest rate — the uncollateralized overnight call rate — at approximately 0.75% [[PDF] April 28, 2026 Bank of Japan Statement on Monetary Policy](https://www.boj.or.jp/en/mopo/mpmdeci/mpr_2026/k260428a.pdf). This was confirmed at the most recent Monetary Policy Meeting on April 27–28, 2026, where the Policy Board voted 6–3 to keep the rate unchanged [[PDF] April 28, 2026 Bank of Japan Statement on Monetary Policy](https://www.boj.or.jp/en/mopo/mpmdeci/mpr_2026/k260428a.pdf). Three dissenting members — Nakagawa Junko, Takata Hajime, and Tamura Naoki — proposed raising the rate to 1.0%, but their proposals were defeated [[PDF] April 28, 2026 Bank of Japan Statement on Monetary Policy](https://www.boj.or.jp/en/mopo/mpmdeci/mpr_2026/k260428a.pdf). This 6–3 split represents the widest division under Governor Ueda's tenure.

Market expectations for a June hike are elevated but uncertain. Reuters reported the BOJ has "locked in" signals for a June rate hike, while nearly two-thirds of Reuters-polled economists expect the rate to reach 1.0% by end-June. However, some economists, such as Oxford Economics' Shigeto Nagai, argue the BOJ will not have sufficient data by June to justify a hike. Polymarket implied probability for a 25 basis point hike stands at approximately 63%.

The next scheduled Monetary Policy Meeting is June 15–16, 2026 (JST). The BOJ publishes its policy decision via the "Statement on Monetary Policy" on the final day of the meeting.
questions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves as **Yes** if the Bank of Japan, in its official "Statement on Monetary Policy" published following the conclusion of the Monetary Policy Meeting on June 15–16, 2026 (JST), announces a guideline for the uncollateralized overnight call rate that is higher than 0.75% (i.e., an increase of at least 1 basis point above the current ~0.75% target). The "Short-Term Policy Interest Rate" refers to the BOJ's guideline for the uncollateralized overnight call rate, as described on the BOJ's monetary policy page (https://www.boj.or.jp/en/mopo/outline/index.htm).

This question resolves as **No** if the BOJ decides to maintain the uncollateralized overnight call rate at approximately 0.75% or lower, or if the June 15–16, 2026 meeting does not take place.

The resolution source is the official "Statement on Monetary Policy" published on the Bank of Japan's Monetary Policy Releases page: https://www.boj.or.jp/en/mopo/mpmdeci/mpr_2026/index.htm

questions.resolution_criteria:

questions.question: Will Japan conduct a live-fire missile exercise outside Japanese territory between May 12, 2026, and July 1, 2026?
questions.background:
On May 6, 2026, Japan's Ground Self-Defense Force (JGSDF) fired two Type 88 surface-to-ship missiles from Philippine territory during the Balikatan 2026 joint military exercise, sinking a decommissioned Philippine Navy vessel (BRP Quezon) approximately 75 km offshore in the Luzon Strait. This marked Japan's first post-WWII offensive missile launch outside Japanese territory and represented a major threshold crossing in Japan's evolving military posture. China condemned the action, with the Global Times calling it "a major and dangerous gamble."

Separately, Japan has announced plans to test U.S.-made Tomahawk cruise missiles from the destroyer JS Chokai in the eastern Pacific during summer 2026, which would constitute another live-fire missile exercise outside Japanese territory.

The question asks whether Japan will conduct an additional such exercise after the Balikatan 2026 firing, signaling that overseas missile employment is becoming a new norm rather than remaining a one-off event. The Tomahawk test and other scheduled bilateral or multilateral exercises (e.g., RIMPAC 2026) make this plausible but not certain within the short window.
questions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves **Yes** if, between May 12, 2026, 00:00 UTC and July 1, 2026, 23:59 UTC, the Japan Self-Defense Forces (JSDF) — including any branch (JGSDF, JMSDF, or JASDF) — conduct at least one live-fire missile exercise outside Japanese territory. This explicitly excludes the Balikatan 2026 Type 88 firing that occurred on May 6, 2026.

**Definitions:**

- **"Live-fire missile exercise"**: The actual launch and flight of a guided missile (not a rocket, bomb, torpedo, or unguided munition) by JSDF personnel or from a JSDF platform. This includes surface-to-ship missiles, surface-to-air missiles, air-to-surface missiles, cruise missiles (e.g., Tomahawk), and anti-ship missiles. Simulated launches, inert training rounds without propulsion, or launches conducted solely by non-Japanese forces do not count. The missile must be launched by JSDF personnel or from a JSDF-operated platform (e.g., a JMSDF destroyer).

- **"Outside Japanese territory"**: The launch must originate from a location outside Japan's sovereign territory as defined under international law, meaning outside Japan's land territory, internal waters, and territorial sea (extending 12 nautical miles from baselines per UNCLOS Article 3). Japan's Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ) beyond the 12 nm territorial sea is considered "outside Japanese territory" for purposes of this question. Launches from Japanese soil or territorial waters do not count.

**Resolution source**: Official Japan Ministry of Defense press releases (https://www.mod.go.jp/en/), credible international news reporting from outlets such as Reuters, AP, Nikkei Asia, or Naval News, or official U.S. Department of Defense announcements (https://www.defense.gov/News/).

questions.question: Will JNIM's blockade of Bamako still be in effect on June 15, 2026?
questions.background: Since September 3, 2025, the al-Qaeda-affiliated group Jama'at Nusrat al-Islam wal-Muslimin (JNIM) has imposed a fuel blockade on Bamako and other cities in southern Mali, causing severe fuel shortages, rolling blackouts, school closures, and economic disruption [Mali fuel blockade - Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mali_fuel_blockade). The blockade eased in early 2026 due to government negotiations and military activity, but JNIM declared a "full blockade" on April 28, 2026, in retaliation for the Malian military junta's April 25 offensive [Mali fuel blockade - Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mali_fuel_blockade). As of mid-May 2026, the blockade remains active, with JNIM controlling key supply routes into the capital. The situation is highly dynamic: the blockade has fluctuated in intensity multiple times, and both military operations and negotiations could alter its status. Foreign embassies have urged citizens to depart, and the crisis represents a major test for Mali's ruling junta.
questions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves **Yes** if, on or after June 15, 2026 (00:00 UTC), at least one of the following international news outlets reports that JNIM is actively restricting or blocking the movement of fuel, food, or commercial goods into Bamako via road routes:

- **Reuters** (https://www.reuters.com/)
- **AFP/France24** (https://www.france24.com/)
- **BBC** (https://www.bbc.com/news)
- **Al Jazeera** (https://www.aljazeera.com/)

For resolution purposes, a "blockade" is defined as JNIM actively and systematically preventing or significantly restricting the passage of commercial vehicles (fuel tankers, food supply trucks, or general cargo) on major roads leading into Bamako, as described in reporting from the above outlets.

The question resolves **No** if:
- Any of the above outlets reports on or after June 15, 2026 (00:00 UTC) that the blockade has been lifted, ended, or is no longer in effect; OR
- None of the above outlets mention an ongoing JNIM blockade of Bamako in any reporting published between June 15, 2026 and June 30, 2026 (23:59 UTC), in which case silence defaults to **No**.

If outlets provide conflicting information, the most recent report from the above sources as of June 30, 2026 (23:59 UTC) will be used for resolution.

questions.question: Will the National Preparedness Level be raised to Level 3 or higher between April 30, 2026 and June 1, 2026?
questions.background:
The [National Preparedness Level](https://www.nifc.gov/fire-information/statistics) (NPL) is a scale from 1 to 5 used by the National Interagency Fire Center (NIFC) to indicate the level of wildland fire activity and demand for firefighting resources across the United States. Level 1 indicates minimal activity, while Level 5 indicates the most extreme nationwide fire activity with maximum resource commitment. The level is assessed and updated regularly by the National Interagency Coordination Center (NICC).

As of April 24, 2026, the National Preparedness Level is 2 [https://www.nifc.gov/fire-information/nfn](https://www.nifc.gov/fire-information/nfn). Earlier in the 2026 fire season, the Southern Area Geographic Area reached Preparedness Level 3 due to regional fire activity, but the national level has remained at 2. Whether the national level reaches 3 depends on significant fire activity occurring across multiple geographic areas simultaneously. Late spring is typically a transitional period—prescribed fire season winds down while early-season wildfires may increase depending on drought conditions and weather patterns.

The current national preparedness level is published on the NIFC National Fire News page at https://www.nifc.gov/fire-information/nfn and in the NICC Situation Report at https://www.nifc.gov/nicc/sitreprt.pdf.
questions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves **Yes** if the National Preparedness Level is reported as 3, 4, or 5 at any point on or after April 30, 2026 (00:00 UTC) through the end of the day on June 1, 2026 (23:59 UTC).

This question resolves **No** if the National Preparedness Level does not reach 3 or higher by the end of the day (23:59 UTC) on June 1, 2026.

The resolution source is the official NIFC National Fire News page (https://www.nifc.gov/fire-information/nfn) or the NICC Situation Report (https://www.nifc.gov/nicc/sitreprt.pdf). If neither source is available, credible reporting from federal wildfire agencies or major news outlets confirming a preparedness level change will suffice.

questions.question: Will the U.S. Senate pass the FY 2026 immigration enforcement reconciliation bill by June 1, 2026?
questions.background:
The U.S. Senate is considering a Fiscal Year 2026 reconciliation package focused on immigration enforcement. On April 23, 2026, the Senate passed a budget resolution (50–48) laying the groundwork for this reconciliation bill, and the House approved it on April 29 (215–211). On May 5, 2026, the Senate Judiciary and Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs (HSGAC) Committees released draft legislative text [CBO Scores FY 2026 Reconciliation at $72 Billion](https://www.crfb.org/blogs/cbo-scores-fy-2026-reconciliation-72-billion).

The Congressional Budget Office (CBO) scored the legislation at approximately $72 billion in added deficit spending over the next decade (about $94 billion including interest) [CBO Scores FY 2026 Reconciliation at $72 Billion](https://www.crfb.org/blogs/cbo-scores-fy-2026-reconciliation-72-billion). The bill includes funding for Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), Customs and Border Protection (CBP), and other law enforcement functions, as well as a controversial $1 billion allocation for Secret Service security upgrades at the White House.

As of May 13, 2026 (UTC), the Senate committees have completed their markups and Republican leadership aims to bring the bill to the Senate floor the week of May 18, 2026, with a target of clearing the package by the end of May [2025 Reconciliation Tracker](https://www.crfb.org/blogs/2025-reconciliation-tracker). President Trump has set a June 1 deadline for passage. However, procedural hurdles remain significant: the bill must survive a vote-a-rama (unlimited amendment votes), potential Byrd Rule challenges from the Senate parliamentarian, and Republican leadership must hold all 50+ Republican votes given unified Democratic opposition. Sens. Lisa Murkowski (R-AK) and Rand Paul (R-KY) voted against the budget resolution, signaling potential defections on the final bill.
questions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves **Yes** if the U.S. Senate passes the FY 2026 immigration enforcement reconciliation bill — the reconciliation legislation drafted by the Senate Judiciary and Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committees, scored by CBO at approximately $72 billion — by a simple majority vote on final passage on the Senate floor. A Vice Presidential tie-breaking vote (under Article I, Section 3 of the U.S. Constitution) counts as passage.

The passage vote must occur on or after May 12, 2026, and no later than 11:59 PM UTC on June 1, 2026.

The question resolves **No** if no such vote occurs by that deadline, or if the bill fails on final passage.

**Resolution source:** The official Senate roll call vote record, available at https://www.senate.gov/legislative/LIS/roll_call_lists/vote_menu_119_2.htm or the bill's page on https://www.congress.gov/.

The bill's progress depends on the number of committee sittings scheduled, the volume of amendments tabled, and broader political dynamics surrounding Northern Ireland legacy issues. The government has legislative tools to expedite the process, but opposition and the complexity of the subject matter have contributed to repeated delays.

questions.question: Will Troy Jackson or Hannah Pingree finish ahead of Shenna Bellows in the 2026 Maine Democratic gubernatorial primary?
questions.background:
The 2026 Maine Democratic gubernatorial primary is scheduled for June 9, 2026. Maine uses Ranked Choice Voting (RCV) for primary elections, a system in which voters rank candidates by preference; if no candidate wins a majority of first-choice votes, the last-place candidate is eliminated and their votes are redistributed according to voters' next preferences, repeating until one candidate achieves a majority (see: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Instant-runoff_voting).

The Democratic field includes several candidates, among them Troy Jackson, Shenna Bellows, and Hannah Pingree [2026 Maine gubernatorial election - Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Maine_gubernatorial_election). A March 2026 poll showed these three tightly clustered: Troy Jackson at 18%, Shenna Bellows at 17%, and Hannah Pingree at 16%. This near-three-way tie among the non-frontrunner tier makes their relative finishing order highly uncertain and sensitive to endorsements, campaign strategy, and RCV transfer dynamics.

Official round-by-round RCV results will be published by the Maine Secretary of State at https://www.maine.gov/sos/elections-voting/election-results-data [Election Results/Data | SOS - Maine.gov](https://www.maine.gov/sos/elections-voting/election-results-data).
questions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves based on the final official results of the Maine Democratic gubernatorial primary held on June 9, 2026 (ET), as published by the Maine Secretary of State at https://www.maine.gov/sos/elections-voting/election-results-data [Election Results/Data | SOS - Maine.gov](https://www.maine.gov/sos/elections-voting/election-results-data).

"Finish ahead of" is defined as follows: a candidate finishes ahead of another if they are eliminated in a later round of the RCV tabulation, or if they win the election. In Maine's RCV system (explained at https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Instant-runoff_voting), candidates are sequentially eliminated from last place; a candidate eliminated in Round 4 finishes ahead of a candidate eliminated in Round 3.

This question resolves **Yes** if, in the official round-by-round RCV tabulation, either Troy Jackson or Hannah Pingree (or both) finishes ahead of Shenna Bellows — i.e., Bellows is eliminated in an earlier round than at least one of Jackson or Pingree, or at least one of Jackson/Pingree wins the primary while Bellows does not.

This question resolves **No** if Shenna Bellows finishes ahead of both Troy Jackson and Hannah Pingree — i.e., both Jackson and Pingree are eliminated in earlier rounds than Bellows.

If any of the three candidates (Jackson, Bellows, Pingree) do not appear on the June 9, 2026 primary ballot, this question resolves **No**.

questions.question: Will the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers issue a solicitation for Phase 2 (dredging) of the Port of Nome Modification Project by June 1, 2026?
questions.background:
The Port of Nome Modification Project is a multi-phase infrastructure initiative managed by the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Alaska District, aimed at creating the nation's first deep-water Arctic port. The project enlarges Nome Harbor's outer basin and creates a new deep-draft basin at minus 40 feet depth. (See USACE project page: https://www.poa.usace.army.mil/Library/Reports-and-Studies/Port-of-Nome-Modification-Project/)

On August 15, 2025, USACE awarded a $399.4 million construction contract to Kiewit Infrastructure West Co. for Phase 1A, which includes a 1,200-foot causeway extension with 600 feet of dock face [USACE awards construction contract for portion of Port of Nome ...](https://www.poa.usace.army.mil/Media/News-Releases/Article/4276752/usace-awards-construction-contract-for-portion-of-port-of-nome-modification-pro/). The project has four planned phases: Phase 1A (awarded), Phase 2 (deep and outer basin dredging), Phase 1B (additional causeway extension and dock), and Phase 3.

As of mid-2025, USACE officials indicated they expected Phase 2 procurement to go out to bid in May 2026, followed by Phase 1B in fiscal year 2028 and Phase 3 later. However, federal infrastructure procurement timelines frequently shift due to funding availability, environmental reviews, and bureaucratic processes. The project has significant strategic importance given growing U.S. Arctic military and commercial interests, and has been highlighted as key to the Trump administration's global ambitions.

As of April 29, 2026, Phase 1A construction is underway. No Phase 2 solicitation or contract award has been confirmed.
questions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves YES if, on or after April 29, 2026 and on or before June 1, 2026 (11:59 PM UTC), the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Alaska District posts either:

1. A formal solicitation (Request for Proposals or Invitation for Bids) for Phase 2 of the Port of Nome Modification Project on SAM.gov (https://sam.gov/), OR
2. A contract award announcement for Phase 2 on the USACE Alaska District news page (https://www.poa.usace.army.mil/Media/News-Releases/).

"Phase 2" refers specifically to the dredging of the deep and outer basins of the Port of Nome, as described in the USACE Port of Nome Modification Project (https://www.poa.usace.army.mil/Library/Reports-and-Studies/Port-of-Nome-Modification-Project/).

A "solicitation" means a formal procurement notice inviting bids or proposals, not a pre-solicitation notice or sources-sought notice.

If neither a solicitation nor a contract award for Phase 2 appears on SAM.gov or the USACE Alaska District news page by June 1, 2026 (11:59 PM UTC), this question resolves NO.

questions.question: Will Donald Trump publicly confirm his attendance at the 52nd G7 summit in Évian by June 1, 2026?
questions.background:
The [52nd G7 summit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/52nd_G7_summit) is scheduled for June 15–17, 2026, in Évian-les-Bains, France [52nd G7 summit - Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/52nd_G7_summit). The summit was originally planned for June 14–16 but was postponed by one day to avoid clashing with Trump's 80th birthday and a UFC event at the White House [52nd G7 summit - Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/52nd_G7_summit). Trump previously refused to attend a G7 emergency meeting in Paris in January 2026 [52nd G7 summit - Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/52nd_G7_summit). The Trump administration also threatened to boycott the summit if South Africa was invited, leading to Kenya being invited instead [52nd G7 summit - Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/52nd_G7_summit).

As of early April 2026, Reuters reported that French President Macron was seeking to lure Trump to attend by offering a post-summit dinner invitation at Versailles, but sources said "it was not yet clear if Trump would be at Evian-les-Bains let alone Versailles." As of May 1, 2026, there is no confirmed public statement from the White House or Trump himself explicitly confirming attendance at the summit. Trump is listed as a participant on the Wikipedia page, but formal confirmation remains uncertain.
questions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves **Yes** if, between May 1, 2026 00:00 UTC and June 1, 2026 23:59 UTC, there is a public confirmation that Donald Trump will attend the [52nd G7 summit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/52nd_G7_summit) in Évian-les-Bains, France (June 15–17, 2026).

A "public confirmation" is defined as any of the following:
1. An official statement published on the [White House Briefing Room](https://www.whitehouse.gov/briefing-room/) explicitly stating Trump will attend the summit;
2. A post on Donald Trump's verified Truth Social or X (Twitter) account explicitly stating he will attend; or
3. A report from at least one of the following news agencies — [Reuters](https://www.reuters.com/), [Associated Press](https://apnews.com/), or [AFP](https://www.afp.com/) — citing official sources (e.g., White House officials, the President himself) confirming Trump's attendance.

The confirmation must be specific to the 52nd G7 summit in Évian (June 15–17, 2026) and must occur on or after May 1, 2026 00:00 UTC. Confirmations made before this date do not count. If no such confirmation is publicly available by June 1, 2026 23:59 UTC, the question resolves **No**.

questions.question: Will the EU formally adopt a 21st sanctions package against Russia by July 1, 2026?
questions.background:
Since Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, the European Union has adopted 20 numbered sanctions packages against Russia. The most recent, the 20th package, was adopted on April 23, 2026, comprising 120 individual listings and targeting energy, the military-industrial complex, trade, financial services, and crypto [Timeline - Packages of sanctions against Russia since February 2022](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/policies/sanctions-against-russia/timeline-packages-sanctions-since-february-2022/). On May 11, 2026, the Foreign Affairs Council added 16 individuals and 7 entities under existing frameworks, but these were routine listings rather than a new numbered package.

The intervals between recent numbered packages have been irregular: the 17th was adopted May 20, 2025; the 18th on July 18, 2025; the 19th on October 23, 2025; and the 20th on April 23, 2026 — intervals ranging from roughly 2 to 6 months [Timeline - Packages of sanctions against Russia since February 2022](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/policies/sanctions-against-russia/timeline-packages-sanctions-since-february-2022/).

EU sanctions require unanimous agreement among all 27 member states in the Council. Hungary and Slovakia have repeatedly complicated or delayed adoption of packages through veto threats, as seen with the prolonged deadlock preceding the 20th package. As of mid-May 2026, multiple credible outlets (Politico, S&P Global, Anadolu Agency) report that the EU is actively preparing a 21st sanctions package focused on Russia's shadow fleet, banks, and defense sector, with a timeline of late June or early July 2026. This makes the outcome genuinely uncertain for a July 1 deadline — the package could slip to after that date due to political negotiations or member-state objections.
questions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves **Yes** if the Council of the European Union formally adopts a package explicitly numbered or designated as the "21st package" (or "21st round") of sanctions against Russia. The formal adoption must occur on or after May 12, 2026, and on or before July 1, 2026 (23:59 UTC).

A "21st sanctions package" is defined as a new numbered comprehensive sanctions package in the series tracked on the official Council of the European Union sanctions timeline page: https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/policies/sanctions-against-russia/timeline-packages-sanctions-since-february-2022/. This is the authoritative source of truth.

Routine individual listings, extensions of existing measures, or additions of persons/entities under existing legal bases (such as the May 11, 2026, FAC additions) do **not** count as a new numbered package. The package must appear as a distinct numbered entry (21st) on the Consilium timeline page linked above.

This question resolves **No** if no such package is formally adopted by 23:59 UTC on July 1, 2026.

questions.question: Will Anthropic publicly disclose at least one zero-day vulnerability found by Claude Mythos Preview (by replacing a SHA-3 hash commitment with a full vulnerability report) by June 1, 2026?
questions.background: On April 7, 2026, Anthropic published a blog post titled "Assessing Claude Mythos Preview's cybersecurity capabilities" at https://red.anthropic.com/2026/mythos-preview/, detailing how their Claude Mythos Preview model discovered numerous zero-day vulnerabilities in major operating systems and browsers [https://red.anthropic.com/2026/mythos-preview/](https://red.anthropic.com/2026/mythos-preview/). The post's Appendix contains 13 SHA-3 hash commitments, each corresponding to a specific vulnerability that Anthropic has reported to affected vendors but cannot yet publicly disclose [https://red.anthropic.com/2026/mythos-preview/](https://red.anthropic.com/2026/mythos-preview/). Anthropic stated they will replace these hash commitments with links to full vulnerability reports once the responsible disclosure process for each vulnerability is complete, which typically follows a 90-day-plus-45-day timeline after initial reporting [https://red.anthropic.com/2026/mythos-preview/](https://red.anthropic.com/2026/mythos-preview/). As of April 30, 2026, all 13 hash commitments remain in place, with none yet replaced by full vulnerability reports. One CVE (CVE-2026-4747) and one GitHub security advisory (GHSA-v782-6fq4-q827) are referenced elsewhere on the page, suggesting at least some disclosure processes are underway [https://red.anthropic.com/2026/mythos-preview/](https://red.anthropic.com/2026/mythos-preview/). The tight timeline—announced April 7, with resolution by June 1—means only vulnerabilities with unusually fast vendor response and patching cycles would be disclosed in time.
questions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves **Yes** if, on or after April 30, 2026 and by 23:59 UTC on June 1, 2026, at least one of the 13 SHA-3 hash commitments listed in the Appendix of the Anthropic blog post at https://red.anthropic.com/2026/mythos-preview/ has been replaced with a full vulnerability report. A "full vulnerability report" is defined as any of the following: (a) a technical write-up published directly on the page in place of the hash, (b) a hyperlink to a CVE entry in the National Vulnerability Database (https://nvd.nist.gov/), (c) a hyperlink to a vendor or third-party security advisory (e.g., a GitHub Security Advisory, a Chrome/Firefox/Windows security bulletin), or (d) a hyperlink to any other publicly accessible document that describes the vulnerability in technical detail (e.g., affected software, attack vector, impact). The replacement must appear on the page at https://red.anthropic.com/2026/mythos-preview/ or on an official Anthropic page directly linked from that Appendix section. The question resolves **No** if all 13 SHA-3 hash commitments remain unreplaced as of 23:59 UTC on June 1, 2026.

Whether the three-judge panel (this is a trial without jury, as is standard for NSL cases) can deliberate and hand down a verdict before July 1, 2026 remains uncertain, as deliberation periods in comparable Hong Kong national security cases have varied from weeks to months.
questions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves **Yes** if a verdict — defined as the oral delivery of a judgment of guilty or not guilty in open court — is delivered for Lee Cheuk-yan and Chow Hang-tung on or after May 12, 2026, and on or before July 1, 2026 (23:59 UTC).

questions.question: Will France be ranked #1 in the FIFA Men's World Rankings as of June 1, 2026 (23:59 UTC)?
questions.background: As of the April 2026 FIFA Men's World Rankings update, France holds the #1 position with 1877.32 points, followed closely by Spain with 1876.4 points and Argentina with 1874.81 points [https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/46664763/fifa-mens-top-50-world-rankings](https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/46664763/fifa-mens-top-50-world-rankings). The FIFA Men's World Ranking uses an Elo-based points system where points are added or subtracted based on match results, match importance, and opponent strength. FIFA introduced real-time live ranking updates in March 2026, meaning any international matches (including pre-World Cup friendlies in late May/early June 2026) can shift the rankings before the next official static release on June 9, 2026. The 2026 FIFA World Cup is scheduled to begin on June 11, 2026, so the rankings as of June 1 represent a key snapshot of team standings heading into the tournament.

If two or more teams have identical point totals (equal to the second decimal place), the team listed higher by FIFA's official ranking page is considered #1.

If the FIFA live ranking tracker is unavailable or non-functional at 23:59 UTC on June 1, 2026, the most recent ranking snapshot available on the official FIFA website prior to that time will be used. If no live data is available, the April 2026 official static rankings (the last static release before the June 9, 2026 update) will be used as the fallback.

questions.question: Will Christophe Gleizes be released from Algerian custody by July 1, 2026?
questions.background:

In June 2025, he was sentenced to seven years in prison for "glorifying terrorism" based on alleged contact with the Movement for the Self-Determination of Kabylie (MAK), designated a terrorist organization by Algeria [https://www.africanews.com/2026/05/08/france-moves-to-repair-ties-with-algeria-as-ambassador-returns-to-algiers/](https://www.africanews.com/2026/05/08/france-moves-to-repair-ties-with-algeria-as-ambassador-returns-to-algiers/). In December 2025, the Tizi Ouzou appeals court upheld the seven-year sentence.

As of May 2026, Franco-Algerian diplomatic relations are experiencing a significant thaw, marked by the return of the French ambassador to Algiers. In early May 2026, Gleizes withdrew his appeal to Algeria's highest court — a move widely interpreted as a necessary procedural step to open the path for a presidential pardon by Algerian President Tebboune [https://www.africanews.com/2026/05/08/france-moves-to-repair-ties-with-algeria-as-ambassador-returns-to-algiers/](https://www.africanews.com/2026/05/08/france-moves-to-repair-ties-with-algeria-as-ambassador-returns-to-algiers/). His case has drawn international attention, with FIFA and press freedom organizations such as CPJ calling for his release.

Despite these positive diplomatic signals, Algeria may choose to retain Gleizes as diplomatic leverage, and domestic political considerations on both sides could delay or complicate a pardon. As of May 13, 2026, Gleizes remains imprisoned in Algeria.
questions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves **Yes** if, on or after May 12, 2026 and by 23:59 UTC on July 1, 2026, Christophe Gleizes is released from Algerian custody. "Released from Algerian custody" means he is no longer imprisoned, detained, or held under house arrest by Algerian authorities. Transfer to French custody (e.g., via extradition or consular transfer) also counts as release from Algerian custody. A presidential pardon, commutation of sentence, or any other legal mechanism resulting in his physical release qualifies.

The withdrawal of his appeal to Algeria's highest court is **not** a necessary condition for resolution; it is background context only. What matters is whether he is physically released from Algerian custody.

This question resolves **No** if Gleizes remains in Algerian custody (prison, detention, or house arrest) as of 23:59 UTC on July 1, 2026.

**Resolution sources:** Credible international news reporting from outlets such as Reuters (https://www.reuters.com), Agence France-Presse, Associated Press, France 24 (https://www.france24.com), BBC (https://www.bbc.com), Le Monde (https://www.lemonde.fr/en/), or official statements from the French or Algerian governments.

questions.question: Will Judge Brinkema issue a remedies ruling in United States v. Google LLC, Case No. 1:23-cv-00108 (E.D. Va.) by June 1, 2026?
questions.background:
On January 24, 2023, the U.S. Department of Justice filed an antitrust lawsuit against Google LLC in the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Virginia, alleging Google illegally monopolized the advertising technology market. On April 17, 2025, Judge Leonie M. Brinkema found that Google violated Section 2 of the Sherman Act by willfully acquiring and maintaining monopoly power in the open-web display publisher ad server market and the open-web display ad exchange market [United States v. Google LLC (2023) - Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_v._Google_LLC_(2023)).

Following this liability finding, the case entered a remedies phase. The remedies trial concluded in late 2025, with closing arguments held on November 21, 2025. The DOJ proposed structural remedies including divestiture of Google's ad exchange, while Google opposed divestiture and proposed behavioral remedies instead.

As of early 2026, multiple sources expected the remedies ruling in Q1 2026, but it had not yet been issued. The Atlantic reported in January 2026 that "Brinkema has yet to rule on the proper remedy for Google's ad-tech monopoly." As of April 8, 2026, the CourtListener docket shows continued filings but no remedies ruling has been entered [United States v. Google LLC, 1:23-cv-00108 – CourtListener.com](https://www.courtlistener.com/docket/66753787/united-states-v-google-llc/). The ruling remains pending as of May 2, 2026.

Resolution source: The official court docket is tracked on CourtListener at https://www.courtlistener.com/docket/66753787/united-states-v-google-llc/ and on PACER for the Eastern District of Virginia.
questions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves **Yes** if, on or after May 1, 2026 and on or before June 1, 2026 (23:59 UTC), Judge Leonie M. Brinkema issues a remedies ruling in United States v. Google LLC, Case No. 1:23-cv-00108 (E.D. Va.). A "remedies ruling" is defined as a memorandum opinion, court order, or final judgment entered on the docket that specifies the structural and/or behavioral requirements imposed on Google LLC as a remedy for the antitrust violations found in the April 17, 2025 liability ruling. Procedural orders (e.g., scheduling orders, discovery orders) do not count.

This question resolves **No** if no such remedies ruling is entered on the docket by June 1, 2026, 23:59 UTC.

If the case is settled or dismissed before a remedies ruling is issued, this question resolves **No**, as no judicial remedies ruling would have been made.

The resolution source is the official court docket for Case No. 1:23-cv-00108 (E.D.
